subject: geography
prompt: Wheat is grown in a village, but most of the people who need it live in a distant city. What makes it possible for the wheat to reach them?

image.alt: A village with farms, a truck on a road and a city, marked supply and demand

hint: Goods and services do not move by themselves.
explanation: Goods do not move from supply locales to demand locales on their own. Movement needs **transport**, and traders make the products reach the consumers. Communication alone carries information, not goods, and local trade cannot serve a distant city.

options.text: The wheat moves from the supply place to the demand place on its own
Transport, with traders who bring the products to consumers
Only communication such as radio and newspapers
Local trade alone, without any movement of goods

subject: geography
prompt: Goods and services move over three important domains (areas) of the earth. On this basis, transport is classified into

image.alt: A plane in the air, a truck and train on land and a ship on water

hint: Think of where the vehicles travel.
explanation: The three domains are **land, water and air**, so transport is land, water and air transport. Local, state and international describe the scale of trade, and road, rail and pipeline are only some forms of transport.

options.text: road, rail and pipeline transport only

subject: geography
prompt: Transport, communication and trade are called complementary. Which statement best explains why?

image.alt: Three pills for transport, communication and trade joined by lines

hint: Each one needs the other two.
explanation: The chapter says transport has made the world a large village with the help of an equally developed communication system, so transport, communication and trade support one another. None of them works alone.

options.text: Fast, efficient transport is achieved with an equally developed communication system, and together they support trade
Trade can grow without any transport if communication is good
Communication makes the movement of goods unnecessary
Only transport matters, and communication and trade follow on their own

subject: geography
prompt: India has about 62.16 lakh km of roads (2020-21). This is the second largest road network in the world. Which statement about roadways is correct?

image.alt: Places A to I joined by a web of roads

hint: Look at the order in which the two modes appeared.
explanation: In India roadways preceded railways, and they still have an edge since they are easier to build and maintain. The network is the **second** largest, and road construction costs much less than railway lines.

options.text: Railways came before roadways in India
Roads cost more to build than railway lines
Roadways preceded railways and still have an edge because roads are easier to build and maintain
India has the largest road network in the world

subject: geography
prompt: The National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) is building six-lane Super Highways. They link four mega cities in a ring, as shown in the diagram. What is their main aim?

image.alt: An abstract ring of four cities A to D joined by six-lane roads and crossed by two long corridors

hint: The Golden Quadrilateral joins the biggest cities.
explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways aim to cut the time and distance between the mega cities. Linking villages with towns is the aim of rural road schemes, state capitals with districts is the job of State Highways, and border areas are the work of the Border Roads Organisation.

options.text: To link every village with a major town by an all-season road
To link a state capital with its district headquarters
To reduce the time and distance between the mega cities of India
To build roads of strategic importance in border areas

subject: geography
prompt: Under the Pradhan Mantri Grameen Sadak Yojana, special provision is made so that

image.alt: A village joined to a town by a road that a truck can use in the rain

explanation: The scheme gives special impetus to "Other Roads", the rural roads. Its aim is an **all-season motorable road** between every village and a major town. The other options describe different road classes.

options.text: every village is linked to a major town by an all-season motorable road
every state capital is joined to a National Highway
every district road becomes a six-lane Super Highway
every border area gets a tunnel

subject: geography
prompt: Metalled roads are made of cement, concrete or bitumen, and they can be used in all weather. Unmetalled roads go out of use in the rainy season. Which picture shows an unmetalled road?
hint: Which road turns to mud and puddles in the rain?
explanation: An unmetalled road has no hard surface, so rain turns it to mud and it goes out of use. Concrete and bitumen roads are metalled and stay usable in the rain.

image.alt: Concrete road with a truck in the rain
Bitumen road with a car in the rain
Muddy road with puddles in the rain
Cement road with a truck on a sunny day

subject: geography
prompt: The Border Roads Organisation built the Atal Tunnel (9.02 km). Before this tunnel, the Manali to Lahul-Spiti valley was cut off for about 6 months of the year. By how many months does the tunnel increase the time the valley can be reached?

image.alt: Twelve month boxes, six blocked by snow before the tunnel and none after

hint: Open time after the tunnel minus open time before.
explanation: Before: 12 - 6 = 6 months open. After: all 12 months open. The gain is 12 - 6 = **6 months**. Choosing 12 mixes up the total with the gain, and 3 wrongly halves the cut-off period.

explanation: The first train steamed off from Mumbai to Thane in **1853**, covering **34 km**. Indian Railways is the largest public sector undertaking and is now reorganised into 17 zones.

subject: geography
prompt: Table 7.1 gives these route lengths: 63,950 km (broad gauge), 2,402 km (metre gauge) and 1,604 km (narrow gauge). The total is 67,956 km. What percentage of the route is broad gauge (to one decimal place)?

image.alt: A stacked bar of broad, metre and narrow gauge route lengths

hint: Divide broad gauge by the total of all three gauges.
explanation: Broad gauge share = 63,950 / 67,956 x 100 = **94.1%**. Traps: dividing by broad + metre only gives 96.4%; the metre-gauge share is 3.5%; dividing by broad + narrow gives 97.6%.

subject: geography
prompt: The five original National Waterways have lengths of 1,620 km, 891 km, 205 km, 1,078 km and 588 km. What is their total length?

image.alt: Bar chart of the lengths of the five National Waterways

hint: Add all five bars of the chart.
explanation: 1,620 + 891 + 205 + 1,078 + 588 = **4,382 km**. Leaving out N.W. 5 gives 3,794, leaving out N.W. 3 gives 4,177. The 14,500 km is the length of all inland navigation waterways, a different figure.

subject: geography

image.alt: A grid of 111 dots, five declared earlier and the rest declared by the 2016 Act

hint: Remove the ones that already existed.
explanation: 111 - 5 = **106**. Choosing 111 forgets that 5 were already declared, and 116 adds instead of subtracting.

subject: geography
prompt: Which mode of transport has no trans-shipment losses and delays (losses and delays from shifting goods between vehicles)?

image.alt: Oil moved by road, rail and ship with transfers marked, compared with one pipeline

hint: There is no loading and unloading in between.
explanation: A pipeline carries oil or gas continuously from source to destination, so nothing is transferred between vehicles. Its initial cost is high, but running costs are minimal.

subject: geography
prompt: India's gas pipeline network grew from 1,700 km (the first HVJ line) to 18,500 km of cross-country pipelines. By how many km did it grow?

image.alt: Two bars of 1,700 km and 18,500 km of gas pipelines

hint: Subtract the starting length from the present length.
explanation: 18,500 - 1,700 = **16,800 km**. Giving 18,500 forgets to subtract, 20,200 adds the two, and 1,700 is only the starting length.

subject: geography
prompt: Waterways are the cheapest, fuel-efficient and environment friendly mode of transport. Which picture shows the kind of cargo they are most suitable for?
hint: Think of heavy and bulky goods.
explanation: Waterways are best for **heavy and bulky goods** such as coal. A small parcel of flowers is better flown, letters go by mail van, and one person with a small bag needs no barge.

image.alt: A parcel of flowers flown by plane
Mail van with letters
A person with a small bag
Barge heaped with coal

subject: geography
prompt: India's sea routes carry 95 per cent of the foreign trade by volume (amount of goods). But by value, they carry only 68 per cent. By value, what percentage of foreign trade is NOT moved by sea?

image.alt: Two bars showing 95 per cent by volume and 68 per cent by value

hint: Work with the value figure, not the volume figure.
explanation: By value the sea carries 68%, so 100 - 68 = **32%** goes by other routes. 5% is the volume figure (100 - 95), 68% is the sea share itself, and 95% is the volume share.

subject: geography
prompt: Kolkata port needs constant dredging (clearing of the river bed). Why? And which port was developed to reduce its growing pressure?

image.alt: A tidal river port with a ship, silt on the river bed and a dredger

hint: Think of what a tidal river does to its bed.
explanation: Shyama Prasad Mookerjee (Kolkata) port is an inland riverine, tidal port on the Hooghly, so it needs constant dredging. **Haldia** was developed as a subsidiary port. Visakhapatnam is the deepest land-locked port and Chennai one of the oldest artificial ports.

options.text: It is on the open sea coast with no river; Paradwip was developed
It is a tidal riverine port on the Hooghly, so silt must be cleared; Haldia was developed as a subsidiary port
It is the deepest land-locked port; Visakhapatnam was developed
It is an artificial port; Chennai was developed

subject: geography
prompt: The Jawaharlal Nehru port was planned mainly to

image.alt: A crowded port and a new hub port taking some of the load

hint: It was built beside an existing crowded port.
explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru port was planned to decongest Mumbai and act as a hub. Iron ore concentrates go from New Mangalore, Haldia relieves Kolkata, and Kandla was built after Partition.

options.text: export iron ore concentrates from the Kudremukh mines
relieve the pressure on the Kolkata port
decongest the Mumbai port and serve as a hub port for the region
replace the port lost to Pakistan at Partition
